reason: As a ledger correction the finding holds. As a 29 Sep candidate it is dead, and the finding does not claim otherwise. (1) The inversion is real. s_merge.json l.486 and l.48 and ideas.json I-034 say the blend is '>= +1.6-2% worse' on 44b6. The source skeptic, v_github-intel_head-blend_schedule.json (3), says 'at most the average ... bound is +1.6..2.0%', which is an upper bound. (2) The numbers match scratchpad r12/blend.log exactly. 6bba->44b6: blend50 +0.03% raw, -0.67% bias-removed; m7 16,820 -> 16,821. 44b6->6bba: blend50 -1.57% / -1.78%; m7 +42 of 102,519. leak5 44b6 is better in 4 of 5 folds, but those folds are in-embryo. (3) The finding overstates one point. The old verdict rested on the pre-registered gate (b): blend <= 0.95x public on EACH embryo. The new measurement RE-CONFIRMS that the gate fails (44b6 +0.03% / -0.67%). The value skeptic's honest variant (<= 0.97x bias-removed in both held-out directions) fails too (-0.67%, -1.78%). So the verdict is right and only the '>=' clause is wrong. (4) This is not new information about value. v_github-intel_head-blend_value.json already predicted -1.3% +-1.5% on an unseen embryo, and the measurement falls inside that range. (5) The claimed +0.0005..+0.0015 public is optimistic. m7 barely moves (0.04%). The slope per 1% came from x138's head gain, which included a node-multiplier share. Coordinate-only riders such as floatout (lab +0.0023) read 0 on the LB twice. The proxy's held-out 'new' head also saw only one embryo (61 or 118 videos), not the 199-video Q head of I-034. (6) The I-033 side correction is valid. R8-RC-A measured +0.00161 lab for a +0.1 voxel z shift, so the metric does not ignore constant offsets. Feasibility: it cannot meet R8 by 27 Sep 12:00 UTC (it needs a headblend patch, a GPU exp60 lab, a dummy and a user OK). It has no finals or E10 impact. The throwaway CPU heads fitted for evaluation break no rule about shipped models, but the user should be told about them.
